Generally I think of the French as cheese-eating surrender-monkeys, but for once they've got a point.
Buying Windows 10 and accepting the EULA means giving consent

Not necessarily, it could be argued that EULAs are representative of contracts of adhesion and are so unconscionable - that is one sided - that they are in violation of uniform commercial code. Most countries have consumer laws which are automatically applied at the point of purchase and as draconian as a EULA could be it could not invalidate these. As well as independent agencies designed to protect the interests of consumers under these same laws, with this article being an example of that process taking place.

Forgive me if I don't go into the legality completely but these issues can get really complex especially when you're talking the operation of different legal systems over different countries. Although that said, even in America the actual legality of EULAs in broad terms has not been held up - as far as I know - and where they have been found to be valid court decisions have been limited to particular provisions and terms found in them.
Forcing windows 10 upgrade at 3 in the morning and then failing to uninstall properly after disagreeing to the terms and conditions isn't exactly consent either.
